title: A smart wristwatch prompts a patient's readmission to the emergency department, where a postoperative pulmonary embolism is investigated and managed (Toronto, 2021)
summary: Orthopedic surgeons at Toronto Western Hospital report that a patient's smart wristwatch, of a brand that the abstract does not name, prompted readmission for a postoperative pulmonary embolism.
account: Drynan, Leroux and Zywiel reported a case in JBJS Case Connector (volume 11, issue 2, April-June 2021). They are from the Division of Orthopedic Surgery, Toronto Western Hospital, University of Toronto. It was published online 8 June 2021. The event date is not available. In the abstract's words, a smart wristwatch prompted a patient's readmission to the emergency department for postoperative pulmonary embolism investigation and management. The abstract adds that constant patient monitoring and alerts are advantages of community-based smart technology. It says that surrounding issues must be considered in implementation. The abstract is the only available account. The patient's age, sex, operation, what the watch measured or alerted, the device's brand, and the clinical outcome are therefore not known.
purpose: Consumer activity monitors are built to track heart rate and activity and to alert the wearer. The abstract credits the watch with prompting the readmission but does not say which function did so.
system: Smart wristwatch / personal activity monitor (brand, model and alert type not stated in the abstract)
developer: Not stated (the abstract does not name the device's maker)
location: Toronto, Canada (authors' institution; the abstract does not state where the case occurred)

brief: In a case report published online on 8 June 2021, Drynan, Leroux and Zywiel of the orthopedic surgery division at Toronto Western Hospital credit a smart wristwatch with prompting a patient's readmission to the emergency department for investigation and management of a postoperative pulmonary embolism. They count constant patient monitoring and alerts among the advantages of community-based smart technology and add that surrounding issues must be considered in implementation. The abstract is the only available account.[1] It does not give the patient's age or sex, the operation, the watch's brand, what the watch measured or the outcome. It does not establish that AI contributed to the patient's care.[2]
